title: Parallel decoding of derived grid tiles can trigger a heap use-after-free
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: When derived HEIF tiles shared a coded input, one thread could query its bit depth while another replaced and freed cached decoder data. A crafted HEIF can trigger heap use-after-free during parallel decoding, causing application crash or heap corruption with default options.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-DTFMOJ5O. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: The fix protects bit-depth queries with the coded input item mutex; fixed in libheif 1.23.7. The issue requires a crafted file and parallel decoding of shared derived inputs. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.
